provenance.notes: Body and leads: Yageo CFR datasheet V.3 (Apr 2024), DIMENSIONS table p.3, row CFR-25 (1/4 W normal style): L 6.3±0.5, ØD 2.4±0.2, lead length H 28±2, lead Ød 0.55±0.05 mm. Power 1/4 W at 70 °C, max working voltage 250 V, max overload 500 V: Table 1 p.3, CFR-25 column (the MFR V.4 sheet gives the same 6.3 x 2.4 mm body and 250/500 V for MFR-25). Tolerance: the 5% grade is carbon-film CFR-25JB; Yageo CFR lists only ±2% and ±5% and Stackpole CF14 (cross-check) only 2% and 5%, so no carbon-film sheet read offers ±1%. The 1% grade is therefore the metal-film Yageo MFR-25FB, which has an identical body. The kit photo shows blue-bodied resistors, which are usually metal film (not verified); SunFounder states no tolerance. Kit quantities from the component-list image: 220 Ω x20, 1 kΩ x10, 10 kΩ x10. Property max 4.7 MΩ is the MFR upper limit (CFR reaches 10 MΩ), so both grades stay valid. Spans: minSpan 1 is an upright mount (body ØD 2.4 stands over one hole, one lead bent back, 2.54 mm apart); a flat mount needs hole spacing above the body length 6.3±0.5 mm (6.8 max), i.e. at least 3 pitches (Yageo's M-type forming uses P = 10.0±1 mm, about 4 pitches). maxSpan 16 = floor((6.3 + 2 x (26 - 8)) / 2.54): 26 mm is the minimum lead length (28 - 2) and 8 mm per lead is an allowance for the bend and hole insertion, which is a modelling assumption and not a datasheet figure. bodyMm is the nominal drawing size [L, ØD, ØD].
